channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Em evento do PT, Lula diz que 'não corre atrás de adversários' e que governo não perderá eleição se fizer ‘as coisas corretas’
item.description: Lula stated that the PT does not chase opponents and will not lose the election if it does 'the right things'. He emphasized that the governing party is pursued by adversaries and expressed confidence in winning the 2026 elections, despite his physical absence due to medical procedures.

item.title: Cármen Lúcia propõe criação de ‘brigadas eleitorais para candidatas mulheres’ nas eleições 2026
item.description: Supreme Federal Tribunal Minister Cármen Lúcia proposed the creation of electoral brigades for female candidates in the 2026 elections, drawing inspiration from the Maria da Penha brigades to combat gender-based political violence. She emphasized that, as former president of the TSE in the 2024 municipal elections, she observed the need for preventive mechanisms to ensure women's safety and full participation in politics. The initiative aims to prevent escalation of violence during campaigns and foster a safer, more democratic electoral environment.

item.title: Por Dentro das Eleições: entenda o que são e como funcionam as mesas receptoras de votos
item.description: The voting polling stations, defined by Resolution 23.751/2026 of the TSE, are the locations where voters will cast their ballots in the 2026 elections, with the first round on October 4 and a possible second round on October 25. Each station consists of a president, first and second poll worker, and a secretary, with preferential convocation of local voters over 18 years old in good standing with the Electoral Justice; in 2024, over 1.9 million people served in these roles. If members are absent, the president must notify the electoral judge, who may authorize reassignment, substitution with logistical support, or appointment of present voters.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes pede desculpas a Romeu Zema após citar homossexualidade
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes admitted he was wrong to mention homosexuality as a possible offense against former governor Romeu Zema during an interview. He apologized to Zema after the comment sparked controversy. Mendes, however, defended his decision to include Zema in the fake news investigation, which probes attacks on the Court.

item.title: Eleições 2026: TRE-SP determina remoção de posts de deputado do PT
item.description: São Paulo’s Electoral Court (TRE-SP) ordered the removal of two paid Facebook posts by state deputy Antonio Donato (PT-SP) for alleged premature electoral campaigning in favor of Fernando Haddad and against Governor Tarcísio de Freitas. Judge Maria Cláudia Bedotti ruled the posts, containing phrases like 'we are going to win this election,' constituted unequivocal electoral propaganda before the legal start date of August 15. Donato’s staff denied receiving notice and claimed Tarcísio is seeking to suppress criticism of a poll showing Haddad close to him.

item.title: Nunes Marques já tem data para assumir a presidência do TSE
item.description: Minister Nunes Marques will assume the presidency of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) on May 12, following the early departure of Minister Cármen Lúcia. He was elected in an administrative session on April 14 and will be joined by Minister André Mendonça as vice-president. The new leadership will oversee the October municipal elections amid growing use of artificial intelligence in the electoral process.

item.title: Gilmar é “ator político” e presta “desserviço”, diz Vieira
item.description: Senator Alessandro Vieira (MDB-AL) labeled Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes a 'political actor' who is doing a 'disservice' to Brazilian justice, in response to Mendes' suggestion that Vieira might be financed by organized crime. Vieira defended the final report of the CPI on Organized Crime, stating it investigates atypical conduct in high institutions, including the Judiciary, and that Mendes' aggressive reaction reveals arrogance and a presumed sense of impunity.

item.title: Em manifesto, PT prevê debate sobre reforma administrativa e do Judiciário
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) will discuss a political manifesto in Brasília to define electoral strategies for 2026 and party guidelines, including proposals for administrative, Judiciary, political, electoral, tax, and technological reforms. The document states these reforms are 'decisive' for the democratic-popular project and warns of the global advance of the far-right. Lula’s participation in the congress closing remains unconfirmed due to a recent medical procedure.

item.title: PGE recomenda inelegibilidade de Carlos Jordy em ação sobre irregularidades durante eleição para Prefeitura de Niterói
item.description: The Electoral Attorney General's Office (PGE) has recommended an eight-year ineligibility for federal deputy Carlos Jordy (PL-RJ) and former vice-mayoral candidate Alexandra da Conceição over alleged irregularities in the 2024 Niterói mayoral campaign, including abuse of power and improper use of communication media. Although the Rio de Janeiro Regional Electoral Court (TRE-RJ) unanimously acquitted them, the case was appealed to the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) by the PDT. Jordy's defense argues the PGE's opinion disregards the evidence and merely repeats the Electoral Public Ministry's claims.

item.title: Moraes manda prender último núcleo de condenados pela trama golpista
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered the definitive execution of sentences for the five convicted members of Nucleus 2 in the Bolsonaro-era coup plot, finalizing the imprisonment of all involved in the attempt to overthrow the Lula government. Sentences range from 8.5 to 26.5 years, including charges of plotting to assassinate Lula, Alckmin, and Moraes, illegal surveillance of the justice, and obstructing voter mobilization. Marília de Alencar will serve 90 days of house arrest with an electronic ankle monitor due to post-surgical recovery.

item.title: Moraes conclui processo da trama golpista
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court concluded the case against five members of the alleged coup plot's management nucleus following the 2022 elections, confirming convictions and ordering the start of sentence enforcement, ranging from 8 years in prison. Justice Alexandre de Moraes formalized the transit in judgment, closing the appeals phase.

item.title: Polymarket e outros sites de apostas preditivas são banidos no Brasil
item.description: The federal government banned the operation of Polymarket and 26 other predictive betting sites in Brazil, declaring them illegal, as part of an effort to curb population indebtedness ahead of the 2026 presidential elections. Announced on Friday (24), the measure aims to prevent speculative practices that could worsen citizens' financial vulnerability during the electoral period.

item.title: Após ser criticado por acordo sobre terras raras com EUA, Caiado diz que Lula 'vende o Brasil'
item.description: Former Goiás governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) criticized President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) for opposing an agreement between Goiás and the U.S. government to explore rare earth minerals and critical minerals. Caiado claimed Lula is the one 'selling Brazil,' arguing the deal offers economic development opportunities for the state. The controversy reflects a national debate over natural resource sovereignty and international partnerships.

item.title: Nikolas Ferreira diz que capacidade cognitiva de filho de Bolsonaro é menor que de ‘toupeira cega’
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) attacked Jair Renan Bolsonaro (PL-SC), the youngest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, claiming his cognitive capacity is lower than that of a 'blind mole'. The exchange occurred on social media after right-wing influencers criticized Ferreira’s appearance and alleged political alignment, including accusations of trading support for amendments. Ferreira has a history of public attacks on Bolsonaro’s sons, including Eduardo Bolsonaro, who stated he can no longer tolerate being humiliated by him.

item.title: Moraes determina prisão de condenados do Núcleo 2 do golpe
item.description: Minister Alexandre de Moraes ordered the imprisonment of five individuals convicted in Núcleo 2 of the Bolsonaro-led coup plot, following the exhaustion of all appeals. The convicted include General Mário Fernandes (26 years and 6 months), Colonel Marcelo Câmara (21 years), Filipe Martins (21 years), former PRF director Silvinei Vasques (24 years and 6 months), and Marília de Alencar (8 years and 6 months), who was granted 90 days of house arrest due to post-surgical recovery. The Supreme Court has convicted 29 individuals in total, with 20 currently in closed regime and Bolsonaro under house arrest.

item.title: PGR diz ao STF ser favorável a pedido de Bolsonaro para realizar cirurgia no ombro
item.description: The Attorney General's Office (PGR) expressed support for the request by former President Jair Bolsonaro's defense to undergo right shoulder surgery, stating there are no legal obstacles to the procedure. Bolsonaro, currently under temporary house arrest, suffers from rotator cuff injuries requiring surgical intervention, according to medical documents. The final decision rests with Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, who authorized the house arrest following hospitalization for bronchopneumonia.

item.title: Motta dá mais um passo para avançar com PEC do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: Speaker of the Chamber of Deputies Hugo Motta has established a special committee to review PEC 221/19, which seeks to end the 6×1 work schedule and reduce the weekly workweek to 36 hours. The committee will consist of 37 titular and 37 substitute members, with up to 40 sessions to issue an opinion. Meanwhile, the Lula government has submitted a constitutional urgency bill to reduce the workweek from 44 to 40 hours, requiring a vote within 45 days or it will block the plenary agenda.

item.title: Manifesto do PT exclui polêmicas e foca na comparação de Lula com Bolsonaro
item.description: The Workers' Party (PT) released the final version of its manifesto for the national congress, removing controversial elements such as the Banco Master case and INSS irregularities involving the president's son, Lulinha. The document now emphasizes a direct comparison between Lula's and Bolsonaro's governments, highlighting Lula's alleged superior crisis management — especially during the Covid-19 pandemic — and mentioning Bolsonaro 15 times. It reinforces the narrative that Lula is the most prepared leader to handle national emergencies.

item.title: Zanin mantém Ricardo Couto como governador do Rio até julgamento do STF sobre nova eleição
item.description: Supreme Court Minister Cristiano Zanin upheld Ricardo Couto as interim governor of Rio de Janeiro until the full court decides whether the next gubernatorial election will be indirect or direct. The ruling was issued on Friday, the 24th, in response to a request for an injunction. Couto, president of the Rio de Janeiro Court of Justice, is serving in the interim role following the resignation of the previous governor.

item.title: PGR se manifesta sobre pedido de nova cirurgia de Bolsonaro
item.description: Attorney General Paulo Gonet expressed support for a new surgery request for Jair Bolsonaro, citing medical evidence of severe right shoulder injuries requiring arthroscopic intervention. He stated there is no legal obstacle to temporarily releasing Bolsonaro from house arrest for the procedure, provided protective measures remain in place, pending final authorization from Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro critica STF por demora em decisão sobre eleição no RJ
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) criticized the STF for delaying the definition of rules for the Rio de Janeiro gubernatorial special election following Cláudio Castro's resignation, accusing the Court of potential bias in favor of Lula's candidate and urging Justice Edson Fachin to act swiftly. He also questioned who would assume governorship if acting governor Ricardo Couto traveled abroad, insisting that elections must be decided by vote, not judicial decree.

item.title: Lula iniciará semana pós-cirurgia em eventos remotos
item.description: President Lula will rest at his São Paulo residence on Saturday (25) following surgery to remove a skin cancer lesion on his head, returning to Brasília on Sunday (26). On Monday (27), he will resume work duties but participate only in previously scheduled events remotely.

item.title: Argentina já tem Polymarket bloqueada desde 16 de março
item.description: Brazil's Central Bank banned predictive markets like Polymarket and Kalshi on April 24, 2026, deeming them illegal for facilitating bets on non-economic events such as elections and reality shows. Argentina had already blocked access to Polymarket since March 16 via a court ruling labeling it an unlicensed online betting system, ordering app removal and restricting registered users. Despite these measures, international platforms remain accessible in Brazil as of the report's publication.

item.title: Cofundadora da Kalshi é brasileira e a mais jovem bilionária do mundo
item.description: Luana Lopes Lara, 29, cofounder of Kalshi and MIT computer science graduate, is the world’s youngest self-made woman billionaire with an estimated net worth of $1.3 billion. Kalshi, a regulated U.S. prediction market platform allowing trades on real-world events like elections and inflation, was blocked in Brazil by the federal government, which ruled its operations fall outside the Betting Law and pose financial risks, particularly to low-income populations. The ban, announced April 24, 2026, targeted 27 prediction market sites with support from the CMN and CVM.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro cobra STF por resolução sobre governo do Rio: ‘Eleição não se resolve em canetada’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) criticized Supreme Court Justice Cristiano Zanin's decision to maintain Rio de Janeiro's Tribunal de Justiça president Ricardo Couto as acting governor, despite the election of Douglas Ruas (PL) as president of the state legislature. Bolsonaro argued that elections should be decided by votes, not judicial rulings, and accused the STF of favoring Lula's candidate. He urged Justice Edson Fachin to prevent the Court from appearing biased.

item.title: STM solicita documentos às Forças Armadas em processo que pode levar à perda de patente de Bolsonaro
item.description: The Superior Military Tribunal has ordered the Armed Forces to submit documents to assess Jair Bolsonaro's conduct following his 27-year and 3-month prison sentence by the STF, in a proceeding that could lead to the revocation of his military rank. The request, made by Bolsonaro's defense and approved by Minister Carlos Vuyk de Aquino, aims to determine whether his behavior undermines the dignity of the officer corps, potentially resulting in a symbolic 'death' and loss of rank if deemed incompatible with military values.

item.title: Após Lula criticar acordo com EUA sobre terras raras, Caiado diz que ele é quem ‘vende o Brasil’
item.description: Former governor Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) rebutted President Lula's criticism, claiming it is Lula who is 'selling Brazil' by exporting raw materials without adding value. Caiado defended the agreement with the U.S. to develop rare earth processing technology in Goiás, arguing it will increase state revenue and technological sovereignty, unlike simply exporting concentrated minerals to China. The March 18 agreement includes $565 million in U.S. funding for Serra Verde, Brazil's only rare earth miner, and while the Goiás government calls it constitutional, experts deem it unconstitutional and beneficial to foreign interests.

item.title: Cartórios ampliam atendimento eleitoral até 6 de maio
item.description: Electoral offices in São Paulo, Minas Gerais, Brasília, Santa Catarina, and Rio de Janeiro are expanding services until May 6 to facilitate voter ID issuance and regularization ahead of the 2026 elections. Services include first-time registration, biometric collection, address transfer, and data updates, with extended hours including weekends and holidays. In-person attendance requires a photo ID and proof of residence, except for those with existing biometrics, who can use the Electoral Justice's online self-service portal.

item.title: Ala do PT reforça fim da 6 x 1 e reforma do Judiciário em documento
item.description: The PT’s majority tendency, Construindo um Novo Brasil, released a document advocating for the end of the 6x1 work schedule, Judiciary reform, and five other structural reforms, alongside a sovereign national project aligned with socialism as a political horizon. The text frames the 2026 elections amid a global rise of the far-right and a civilizational crisis, stressing the need to counter reactionary forces fueled by misinformation and fear. Internally, it calls for strengthening party bases, internal renewal, greater women’s participation, and term limits for party positions.

item.title: Romeu Zema volta a bater em Gilmar Mendes
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) renewed his attacks on Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes after being included in the fake news inquiry over a video criticizing Mendes for annulling a decision to break the secrecy of a company linked to Justice Dias Toffoli's family. Zema stated he sees no issue in calling for investigations against Supreme Court ministers, questioning why some are considered 'untouchable' while he, as a businessman, is subject to normal scrutiny.

item.title: Caiado defende petróleo na Margem Equatorial e sugere crítica à reinjeção do gás natural
item.description: Presidential pre-candidate Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) advocated for oil exploration in the Equatorial Margin and emphasized the need to expand Brazil’s natural gas pipeline infrastructure. He also criticized the reinjection of natural gas, suggesting it is inefficient or inadequate for the country’s energy development.

item.title: Campanha do TSE voltada a jovens é finalista do 4º Prêmio Social Media Gov
item.description: The TSE's 'Voting is Our Thing' campaign, launched in November 2025, is a finalist in the 4th Social Media Gov Award for mobilizing 15- to 17-year-olds to register to vote, supported by influencers like Alok, Mítico and Igão, leading to a 12.8% increase in youth voter registration.

item.title: “Eleição se resolve no voto, não na canetada”, diz Flávio a Fachin sobre Rio
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) criticized STF Minister Cristiano Zanin’s decision to keep Ricardo Couto as acting governor of Rio de Janeiro, stating that elections should be decided by vote, not judicial rulings. He urged STF President Edson Fachin to intervene and uphold the state’s electoral process.

item.title: Gleisi chama conselheiro de Trump de 'misógino de extrema direita' após fala sobre mulheres brasileiras
item.description: Federal deputy Gleisi Hoffmann (PT-PR) called U.S. Special Envoy for Global Affairs Paolo Zampolli an 'arrogant misogynist of the far right' after he claimed in an RAI interview that Brazilian women are a 'cursed race' and 'programmed to cause chaos'. Hoffmann defended respect for Brazilian women and stated Zampolli is 'not welcome' in Brazil, linking the incident to a government strategy to reinforce national sovereignty rhetoric following U.S. tensions over the detention of former deputy Alexandre Ramagem.

item.title: Ao vivo: Edinho Silva e Jilmar Tatto participam de Congresso do PT
item.description: PT president Edinho Silva and vice-president Jilmar Tatto attended the opening session of the party's 8th National Congress in Brasília, under the theme 'Sovereignty, Reconstruction and Future'. The event discussed the political landscape and electoral strategy for 2026, featuring panels on education and elections. The official opening took place at 7 PM at the Brasília 21 Convention Center.

item.title: Gilmar Mendes quer reafirmar quem governa o STF e que inexiste autoridade para investigar ministros
item.description: Gilmar Mendes defends the STF's autonomy and rejects any investigation into its ministers, arguing that inquiries into individual conduct constitute attacks on the institution. He asserts that the fake news inquiry, led by Alexandre de Moraes, is a necessary and permanent tool intended to last at least until the 2026 elections to punish politicians who criticize Supreme Court justices. Mendes positions himself as the leader of a bloc within the STF seeking to shield the Court from external scrutiny, equating political criticism with crime and denying ministers' personal accountability for private relationships.

item.title: Governo veta Kalshi e Polymarket no Brasil
item.description: Brazil's Central Bank banned the offering and trading of prediction contracts tied to political and electoral events, impacting international platforms like Kalshi and Polymarket. The CMN resolution takes effect on May 4 and aims to prevent betting on election outcomes and other sensitive events.

item.title: Nikolas chama Jair Renan, filho de Bolsonaro, de ‘toupeira cega’
item.description: Federal deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) called Jair Renan Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, a 'blind mole' in a social media exchange. The conflict began after an influencer mocked Nikolas for changing from a black to a white shirt, which he interpreted as criticism of his opposition to the Lula government. The exchange of insults is part of a broader pattern of public clashes between Nikolas and other far-right figures, including recent criticisms from Eduardo Bolsonaro.

item.title: Desaprovação de Lula se mantém em 50% no Lulômetro
item.description: President Lula's disapproval rating remained at 50% on Friday, 24, according to the Lulômetro, a daily tracking poll conducted by O Antagonista and Real Time Big Data. This marks the second consecutive day the disapproval rate reached 50%, after first hitting that level on Thursday. The government is rated as "bad/terrible" by 50%, "good/excellent" by 26%, and "fair" by 23%.

item.title: Presidente do PT defende ampliar participação da sociedade no CNJ
item.description: Edinho Silva, president of the Workers' Party (PT), advocated for increasing civil society participation in the National Council of Justice (CNJ) to bring the judiciary closer to Brazilian society, while criticizing 'penduricalhos' as unjustified privileges. He also stressed the need for political-electoral reform, praised the Lula government's economic reforms — including the Tax Reform and fiscal deficit reduction — and defended a national program for rare earth minerals as a matter of national sovereignty, accusing the Bolsonaro family of seeking to hand over such reserves to the United States.

item.title: Forças Armadas devem enviar documentos em processo sobre perda de patente de Bolsonaro
item.description: The Superior Military Tribunal has authorized the collection of documents from the Armed Forces to assess whether former President Jair Bolsonaro should lose his military rank of captain due to his conviction for attempting a coup. The process, based on the STF's ruling, examines alleged violations of military ethics and also includes other officials such as Almir Garnier and Augusto Heleno. The defense has the right to produce evidence, and the trial will proceed after the evidence-gathering phase.

item.title: Saiba quais são as 27 plataformas proibidas de operar no Brasil
item.description: The Brazilian government banned 27 predictive market platforms for violating national legislation, with Anatel initiating access blocks nationwide. These platforms allowed betting on elections, sports, and reality shows, deemed illegal as they do not fit under gambling laws, financial regulations, or derivatives frameworks. The move aims to protect users, particularly low-income individuals, from financial risks due to lack of oversight and regulation.

item.title: A estratégia da oposição para tentar ditar ritmo mais lento da PEC do fim da escala 6×1
item.description: The opposition is seeking to slow the progress of the PEC to end the 6×1 work scale, fearing its approval would boost Lula’s 2026 presidential prospects, particularly against Flávio Bolsonaro. Their strategy includes negotiating compensation for business owners and extending debate in the special committee to the maximum 40 sessions, though this faces opposition from Chamber President Hugo Motta, who favors a swift approval by May.

item.title: Moraes decreta prisão domiciliar de condenada pela trama golpista
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ordered former federal police delegate Marília Ferreira de Alencar to begin serving house arrest for her role in the 2022 coup plot’s Nucleus 2. She was sentenced to eight years and six months for preparing intelligence reports used to target PRF operations in municipalities where Lula received over 75% of the vote, aiming to suppress voter turnout. During the 2022 election period, Marília served as Intelligence Director at the Justice Ministry under Anderson Torres, later following him to the DF Public Security Secretariat.

item.title: O duro documento da Fazenda sobre o ‘mercado de previsões’ no Brasil
item.description: The Brazilian Ministry of Finance, through the Secretariat of Prizes and Bets (SPA), issued a technical note warning of risks such as manipulation, insider information use, money laundering, and terrorism financing in 'prediction markets', particularly those involving non-financial topics like elections. The document states these markets are more susceptible to illicit activities than sports betting due to weak KYC, transaction monitoring, and traceability, and that betting on electoral outcomes constitutes an electoral offense under TSE rulings, threatening democratic integrity.

item.title: PT promete passe livre e fim do Tigrinho na campanha de Lula
item.description: The Workers' Party discussed in Brasília the first version of a document proposing policy guidelines for Lula's 2026 re-election campaign, including free public transportation and restrictions on virtual gambling games like 'Tigrinho'. The draft is still subject to amendments and forms part of the PT's preparation for the upcoming election.

item.title: Congresso decide no dia 30 se mantém veto à dosimetria
item.description: The National Congress will decide on April 30 whether to uphold or overturn the presidential veto on PL 2.162/2023, which established sentencing guidelines for those involved in the January 8, 2023 attacks. President Lula vetoed the bill, arguing that reducing penalties for crimes against the democratic state would violate the Constitution and encourage further antidemocratic acts. Overturning the veto requires an absolute majority in separate votes in the Chamber of Deputies and the Senate.

item.title: Nikolas chama Jair Renan de ‘toupeira cega’ e amplia atrito com família Bolsonaro após embate com Eduardo
item.description: Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) intensified his rift with the Bolsonaro family by calling councilman Jair Renan Bolsonaro a 'blind mole' in a social media exchange, following criticism from Eduardo Bolsonaro and allies over his limited engagement in Flávio Bolsonaro’s pre-campaign. Nikolas claimed he faces 'unilateral attacks' and denied avoiding support for Flávio to avoid sharing the spotlight, stating his strategy is to reach beyond the Bolsonarist base.

item.title: Motta cria comissão para analisar PEC da redução da escala 6X1
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta has created a special committee to analyze two PECs aimed at reducing Brazil's workweek and ending the 6x1 schedule. The proposals include reducing weekly hours from 44 to 36 (Reginaldo Lopes) and implementing a four-day workweek with a 36-hour limit (Erika Hilton). The Lula government has also sent an urgent bill to reduce the workweek to 40 hours, seeking to preempt the PECs' lengthy process.

item.title: Trama golpista: STF encerra fase de recursos e já executou as penas de todos os condenados
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) concluded the appeals phase and ordered the execution of sentences for the 29 individuals convicted of the 2022 coup attempt led by Jair Bolsonaro. Of the convicted, 20 are in closed regime, 3 under house arrest, 3 are fugitives, 2 reached plea deals, and 1 is in open regime. Sentences range from 1 year and 11 months to 27 years and three months, including former ministers and high-ranking military officials.
